verify.text:
**Does another method give the same value?**

| Method | Value |
| --- | --- |
| networkx `maximum_flow` (the **flow** Card) | 9 |
| networkx `minimum_cut` (the **cut** Card) | 9 |
| scipy `maximum_flow` (another implementation) | 9 |
| Brute force over all cuts (512) | 9 |

**There are 2 minimum cuts** (the nodes on the $s$ side of each):

- {s, a1, a3, b3}
- {s, a1, a2, a3, b3}

whatif.text:
**Raising a capacity by 10** (maximum flow was 9)

| Change | On the cut | Flow/capacity | Maximum flow | Gain | New cut |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| none | | | 9 | | a1→b1, a2→b2, b3→c3 |
| a1→b1 | yes | 1/1 | 19 | +10 | a1→b1, a2→b2, b3→c3 |
| s→a2 | no | 6/6 | 9 | +0 | a1→b1, a2→b2, b3→c3 |
| a2→b2 | yes | 6/6 | 9 | +0 | s→a2, a1→b1, b3→c3 |

**Why**: the maximum flow cannot exceed the capacity of any cut. Raising an edge off the cut leaves the original cut's capacity the same, so Even an edge running at full capacity does not increase the maximum flow.
a1→b1 gained as much as it was raised. Raise it further and another cut will get in the way sooner or later.
a2→b2 is on the cut, but another minimum cut without this edge remains, so nothing is gained.
